answer: Each agent registers by submitting an attestation from a secure enclave whose private key is fused into the chip at manufacture; the ledger stores that key and rejects any second identity with the same key, so an attacker cannot forge software identities and must buy one physical enclave chip per fake agent. At roughly forty dollars per chip, building an ocean of sybils costs forty dollars each, making mass fakery unprofitable unless a fake earns more than that before being banned; the umber serial box is irrelevant, only the fused key counts.
